sources.title: Rulebook on entry and stay of aliens
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry hosts this Rulebook on its official domain. Its border-visa provision describes an individual urgent exception tied to a justified reason for failing to apply timely at a diplomatic-consular mission, rather than a nationality-based arrival-visa schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Border visa shall be issued individually to a foreigner in case of urgent entry.

policies.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: A traveller on an ordinary Bosnia and Herzegovina passport is classified as a BiH citizen, not as a foreign visitor under the visa regime.
conditions: The Border Police says a BiH citizen who also holds another citizenship is not considered a foreigner in BiH.
This classification does not establish documentation for a dual national travelling on another passport, work, residence, transit or final border-control treatment.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free visitor baseline
policies.summary: The MFA's individually selected current country results expressly waive the visa requirement for these ordinary-passport nationalities.
conditions: This is a nationality-and-ordinary-passport visitor baseline only. The current individual MFA results state their own maximum stay periods; this grouped policy deliberately does not erase those differences by inventing one shared duration.
It does not establish work, long stay, residence, transit, asylum, emergency, diplomatic, official/service, seaman, identity-card or other special-document treatment.

The Border Police separately permits EU, Schengen, Albanian, Andorran, Montenegrin, Liechtenstein, North Macedonian, Monacan, San Marinese, Serbian, Holy See and Swiss citizens to use a qualifying identity card; that is a document route outside this ordinary-passport policy.

Foreign entry still requires an accepted travel document, generally valid at least three months beyond departure and issued within ten years or permanently; security, purpose, means, document, refusal and final-admission checks remain applicable.

policies.title: United Arab Emirates ordinary passport: visa-free with six-month passport validity
policies.summary: The live MFA UAE result exempts qualifying ordinary passports from the visa requirement for up to 90 days in any 180 days.
conditions: The UAE result requires an ordinary passport valid for at least six months; it also separately mentions diplomatic, special and service passports, which are outside this policy.
The stated visit maximum is 90 days in any 180-day period preceding each day of stay.
Work, residence, transit, final admission and other entry conditions remain outside this visitor baseline.

policies.title: Brazil ordinary passport: visa-free with annual cap
policies.summary: The live MFA Brazil result exempts valid ordinary Brazilian passports for a period not exceeding 90 days, subject to a total annual 180-day cap from first entry.
conditions: The exemption applies to holders of valid ordinary passports and covers entry, exit, transit and stay; the page separately addresses diplomatic and service passports.
The total stay may not exceed 180 days annually, calculated from first entry.
Work, residence, final admission and other general entry requirements remain outside this visitor baseline.

policies.title: Russian Federation ordinary passport: visa-free up to 30 days in each 60-day period
policies.summary: The live MFA Russian Federation result applies the in-force bilateral ordinary-passport visa waiver for stays not exceeding 30 days in every 60-day period from first entry.
conditions: The policy covers the ordinary passport baseline. The result separately names seaman and return-document cases, diplomatic/service passports, and Russian holders of temporary or permanent BiH residence permission; those are not normalized here.
Employment, study and similar purposes require a visa under the published bilateral rule.
General document and final-admission requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Ukraine ordinary passport: visa-free up to 30 days in two months
policies.summary: The live MFA Ukraine result applies the bilateral short-travel waiver to a valid ordinary Ukrainian passport for a period not exceeding 30 days in two months from first entry.
conditions: The result separately covers child travel documents and seaman's books, as well as diplomatic and service passports; those are outside this ordinary-passport policy.
The result frames this as short travel only; work, residence and final admission remain outside the policy.

policies.title: People's Republic of China ordinary passport: visa-free up to 90 days in 180 days
policies.summary: The MFA's live China result expressly exempts valid ordinary People's Republic of China passports for entry, exit, stay or transit up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
conditions: A visa must be obtained before entry for a stay over 90 days or for study, employment, media activity or other pre-approved activities.
Diplomatic, service and public-affairs passports are separately described and are outside this ordinary-passport policy.
General document and final-admission requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports: visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA's live China result expressly exempts passports issued by the Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Regions of the People's Republic of China for up to 90 days in six months from first entry.
conditions: This is document-specific to passports issued by the named PRC Special Administrative Regions; it must not be generalized to other Chinese documents or citizenship categories.
Work, residence, transit, final admission and other entry conditions remain outside this visitor baseline.

policies.title: Taiwan passport carrying a personal identity-card number: visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA's live China result expressly limits Taiwan passport visa exemption to a passport containing the holder's personal identity-card number.
conditions: The exemption is conditional on the personal identity-card number appearing in the passport and is limited to 90 days in six months from first entry.
A Taiwan passport lacking that identifier, work, residence, transit and final-admission treatment are not established by this policy.

policies.title: Bahrain, Oman and Saudi Arabia ordinary passports: temporary visa-free entry through 30 September 2026
policies.summary: Official Gazette 37/26 temporarily exempts ordinary passport holders of Bahrain, Oman and Saudi Arabia from a visa for entry, exit, transit and stay from 1 June through 30 September 2026.
conditions: The exemption applies only to ordinary passports and permits a total stay of up to 60 days within the stated temporary period.
It does not establish a post-30-September-2026 rule, work, residence, special passports, final border admission or other entry conditions.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visitor visa required baseline
policies.summary: The MFA's individually selected current country results expressly require a Bosnia and Herzegovina visa for these ordinary-passport nationalities. This is a consular-visa baseline, not an eVisa or standard visa-on-arrival cohort.
conditions: This is the ordinary national-passport short-visitor baseline. The current MFA selector commonly identifies the responsible BiH diplomatic-consular mission; research found no current official source establishing a nationality-wide electronically issued visa or standard visa-on-arrival entitlement for this group.

Article 17 of the Ministry-hosted Decision on Visas provides a separate, document-conditioned exception: a national otherwise subject to the visa regime may enter without a BiH visa only with a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa, EU-member-state visa, or qualifying Schengen/EU residence permit, subject to its stated limits. It does not alter this nationality baseline.

Diplomatic, official/service, special, refugee, emergency, seaman, residence, work, airport-transit and other travel-document categories are outside this policy. A border visa is not normalized: the Ministry's rulebook describes it as an individual urgent exception, not a nationality-based VOA.
Visa issuance and entry remain subject to accepted-document, purpose, means, security, refusal, sanctions, health and final border-admission checks.

unresolved.reason: Kosovo is absent from the current MFA's individual-country selector. The reviewed current Border Police material and official visa sources do not expressly classify an ordinary Kosovo passport; neither a citizenship/recognition conclusion nor a visa result may be inferred from that silence.
